reproduction_target: Computational analysis of the CLAMP heat-stress 3D-chromatin study: SLAM-seq nascent-RNA differential expression (nf-core/slamseq -> DESeq2), Micro-C differential chromatin interactions (HiC-Pro -> HiCcompare), HiChIP loop calling (BWA/pairtools/cooler -> FitHiChIP/MACS2/edgeR), APA (coolpup.py), and cross-assay integration of Micro-C/HiChIP/SLAM-seq (bedtools + custom Python), plus reuse of public ChIP-seq (deeptools).
granularity_note: Coarse one-step-per-named-tool from Methods 'Computational analysis' (a) SLAM-seq, (b) Micro-C, (c) HiChIP, (d) integration, (e) ChIP-seq. Only third-party tool repos named (nf-core/slamseq, ay-lab/FitHiChIP, dovetail-genomics/HiChiP, nservant/HiC-Pro); NO author-owned analysis-code repository and NO Code Availability statement. Repos not read at line level (stage-1 prose-only). Wet-lab library generation counted in W, not verdicted.

steps.label: nf-core/slamseq v1.0.0 pipeline (-profile singularity; internally Trim Galore 0.6.5 + SlamDunk 0.4.3; full params: --genome BDGP6 --read_length 150 --trim5 12 --polyA 4 --multimappers true --min_coverage 2 --var_fraction 0.2 --conversions 1 --base_quality 27 --pvalue 0.05) — SLAM-seq processing
DESeq2 (1.22.1) — SLAM-seq differential expression (padj <= 0.05, fold change >= 1.5)
HiC-Pro toolkit (3.1.0, default params) + cooler-format conversion utils (nservant/HiC-Pro/bin/utils) — Micro-C mapping and normalized contact maps
HiCcompare (1.24.0) in Bioconductor (3.18) — Micro-C differential chromatin interactions (P < 0.01)
Burrows-Wheeler Aligner (0.7.17) mem — HiChIP (and ChIP-seq) alignment to dm6 (args -5 -S -P -T0 for HiChIP; default for ChIP)
pairtools (0.3.0) parse/dedup/split — HiChIP valid ligation events (--min-mapq 40 --walks-policy 5unique --max-inter-align-gap 30)
cooler suite (0.9.3) — HiChIP/Micro-C contact-map generation from pair files
FitHiChIP (10.0) — HiChIP loop calling (ay-lab/FitHiChIP; resolution-adjustable interaction categories)
MACS2 (2.2.9.1) — 1D peak calling on HiChIP data (required input for FitHiChIP)
edgeR (no version given) in custom scripts located in the FitHiChIP repository — differential loops between conditions
coolpup.py suite (1.0.0) — APA plots over differential loop focal points (central bin 2.5 kb)
bedtools suite (2.31.0, pairtobed) + custom Python annotation script — Micro-C/HiChIP loop-anchor & loop-span gene annotation and SLAM-seq integration (custom script NOT deposited)
matplotlib-venn (0.11.9) Python package + Fisher's Exact test with FDR correction — cross-assay gene-list overlap significance (custom analysis, NOT deposited)
deeptools suite (3.2.1) bamCoverage — public ChIP-seq BigWig tracks (--binSize 50 --normalizeUsing CPM --extendReads 200 --exactScaling --centerReads --blackListFileName dm6-blacklist.bed)
Trim Galore (0.5.0) — public ChIP-seq adapter/quality trimming (GSE118047, GSE30740, GSE36374, GSE36393, GSE54529, GSE63518, GSE80702, GSE89244)
coolbox API (0.3.9) — visualization of contact maps, bigwig/ChIP/nascent-RNA tracks and cross-dataset comparison over regions of interest

headline.inference_inclusive_upper_bound: RI ceiling on 14/17 computational steps; 3/17 (C11 edgeR unversioned, C13 custom bedtools/Python integration script undeposited, C14 custom matplotlib-venn/Fisher overlap script undeposited) cap at NI. R★ not assignable at stage1. Even if stage2 confirms the nf-core/slamseq singularity container resolves to a complete lock (C1), the newly generated GEO series remain PRIVATE/embargoed at assessment time, so most steps cannot yet be executed end-to-end; and the absence of an author code repository / Code Availability statement means the custom integration steps (C13/C14) cannot exceed NI regardless.
headline.coverage: 17 computational steps assessed from Methods prose + repo landing pages; 4 wet-lab library-generation procedures counted (W) but out of computational-reproduction scope.

gaps.where: Newly generated primary data: SLAM-seq (GSE297379), HiChIP (GSE253644), and the poly(T)/nascent series (GSE253645)
gaps.missing: All three GEO Series are still PRIVATE/embargoed (reviewer-token access only) at assessment time; raw/processed files are not publicly downloadable, so the SLAM-seq, Micro-C, and HiChIP computational steps cannot be executed on the study's own data yet.
gaps.how_to_close: Release the GEO Series to public (or provide reviewer tokens) and confirm processed-file availability (contact maps, .cool/.hic, counts) plus a run-to-sample sheet.

gaps.where: Software environment capture across the pipeline
gaps.missing: Only the SLAM-seq step claims a containerized environment (nf-core/slamseq v1.0.0 -profile singularity — env_lock CLAIM, no digest in prose). All Micro-C/HiChIP/ChIP tools are exact-version-pinned in prose but with NO lockfile, container, or OS/library closure; system-library closure unchecked.
gaps.how_to_close: Ship a container digest or conda-lock/pixi.lock covering the non-nf-core tools (HiC-Pro, cooler, HiCcompare/Bioconductor, BWA, pairtools, FitHiChIP, MACS2, coolpup.py, deeptools) for a declared platform; stage2 should resolve the nf-core singularity profile to a concrete pinned container set.

gaps.where: Author analysis code / Code Availability statement
gaps.missing: No Code Availability statement and no author-owned repository. 'Custom scripts' for differential loops (edgeR) are said to live in the third-party FitHiChIP repo; the cross-assay integration/annotation (custom Python + bedtools) and overlap significance (matplotlib-venn + Fisher/FDR) scripts are described but not deposited anywhere.
gaps.how_to_close: Deposit the custom Python/R integration and figure scripts (Zenodo/GitHub with a release tag) and add an explicit Code Availability statement pinning edgeR and all custom-script dependency versions.

gaps.where: Wet-lab generation: RNAi/Kc-cell culture, SLAM-seq 4SU labeling + Lexogen library prep, Micro-C, Dovetail HiChIP MNase library prep + anti-CLAMP IP
gaps.missing: Wet-lab steps are out of scope for computational reproduction (OOS); counted in W, not verdicted.
gaps.how_to_close: N/A for Tier-1 computational readiness; scope is the downstream bioinformatic analysis.
